name: UpperTheory.V.PropA.qzInj
source: ∀ (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime], Module.Injective ℤ_[l] (QZ l) := by
have hmem : ∀ x ∈ I, ∃ c : ℤ_[l], c • a = x := fun x hx =>
have haI : a ∈ I := ha ▸ Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self a
have hy : ∃ y : QZ l, a • y = g ⟨a, haI⟩ := by
refine ⟨LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℤ_[l] (QZ l) y, fun x hx => ?_⟩
have : (⟨c • a, hx⟩ : I) = c • (⟨a, haI⟩ : I) := rfl
rw [this, map_smul g, ← hy, LinearMap.toSpanSingleton_apply, smul_eq_mul, mul_smul]
show: The ℓ-primary character module QZ is injective as a module over the ℓ-adic integers.
strategy: Apply Baer’s criterion to a functional g on a principal ideal (a). Choose a value y for the extension at 1 such that ay=g(a). Divisibility of QZ supplies y if a is nonzero, and y=0 works if a=0.

steps.claim: Put $T=\mathbf Q_\ell/\mathbf Z_\ell$. By Baer's criterion, injectivity follows if every linear $g:I\to T$ extends from an ideal $I$ to $\mathbf Z_\ell$. As $\mathbf Z_\ell$ is a principal ideal ring, choose $a$ with $I=(a)$.
steps.snippet:
∀ (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime], Module.Injective ℤ_[l] (QZ l) := by
  intro l _
  refine Module.Baer.injective ?_
  intro I g
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := (IsPrincipalIdealRing.principal I).principal

steps.claim: Every $x\in I$ has the form $ca$ for some $c\in\mathbf Z_\ell$, since $I$ is the ideal generated by $a$.
steps.snippet:
have hmem : ∀ x ∈ I, ∃ c : ℤ_[l], c • a = x := fun x hx =>
    Submodule.mem_span_singleton.1 (ha ▸ hx)
steps.typedFact: ∀ x ∈ I, ∃ c : ℤ_[l], c • a = x

steps.claim: The generator $a$ itself belongs to $I=(a)$ because $a=1\cdot a$, so $g(a)$ is defined.
steps.snippet: have haI : a ∈ I := ha ▸ Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self a

steps.claim: There exists $y\in T$ with $ay=g(a)$. For $a=0$ take $y=0$, and for $a\ne0$ use divisibility of $T$.
steps.snippet: have hy : ∃ y : QZ l, a • y = g ⟨a, haI⟩ := by
steps.typedFact: ∃ y : QZ l, a • y = g ⟨a, haI⟩

children.claim: The equation $ay=g(a)$ has a zero right-hand side if $a=0$. For nonzero $a$, multiplication by $a$ on $T$ is surjective.
Choose the zero class $y=0$ in $T$ for the zero-generator case. Its scalar multiple $ay$ is zero.
When $a=0$ in the ring, the element $a$ regarded as a member of the ideal $I$ equals the zero element of that ideal.
Linearity gives $g(a)=g(0)=0$, and scalar multiplication gives $a\cdot0=0$, verifying the equation.
If $a\ne0$, divisibility of $T$ gives a preimage $y$ of $g(a)$ under multiplication by $a$. A representative of $g(a)$ in $\mathbf Q_\ell$ can be divided by $a$ to obtain such a class.

steps.claim: Choose $y$ with $ay=g(a)$ and define $G:\mathbf Z_\ell\to T$ by $G(z)=zy$. Since $I=(a)$, every input on which $G$ must agree with $g$ has the form $ca$.
steps.snippet:
obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hy
  refine ⟨LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℤ_[l] (QZ l) y, fun x hx => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := hmem x hx

steps.claim: The element represented by $ca$ in $I$ is the scalar $c$ times the element represented by $a$ because the ideal uses the ring's scalar multiplication.
steps.snippet: have : (⟨c • a, hx⟩ : I) = c • (⟨a, haI⟩ : I) := rfl
steps.typedFact: (⟨c • a, hx⟩ : I) = c • (⟨a, haI⟩ : I)

steps.claim: For every $ca\in I$, $G(ca)=(ca)y=c(ay)=c\,g(a)=g(ca)$. This extends $g$ and establishes the property required by Baer's criterion.
steps.snippet: rw [this, map_smul g, ← hy, LinearMap.toSpanSingleton_apply, smul_eq_mul, mul_smul]

chapterTitle: Twisted cokernels in a cyclotomic tower
